name: PulseBar System Monitor
subtitle: CPU, memory, disk and network
promotionalText: Three configurable rings. The numbers you choose. See CPU, memory, disk and network from your menu bar, with live charts and optional helper insights.
description:
Keep your Mac’s performance within reach. PulseBar brings CPU, memory, disk, and network readings to your menu bar, with a compact overview and focused detail windows.

• Follow CPU and memory usage, memory pressure, swap, storage capacity, disk reads and writes, and upload/download rates.
• View supported GPU utilization and internal-battery information when available on your Mac.
• Inspect live history charts and choose refresh intervals from 1 to 60 seconds.
• Review local performance events for sustained high CPU usage or elevated memory pressure. Optional notifications are off by default.
• Customize three menu bar rings, show rings and numbers separately, and select upload, download, disk read, and disk write independently. Use English or Simplified Chinese.

YOUR MENU BAR, YOUR CHOICE
• Three concentric rings default to storage outside, memory in the middle, and CPU inside. Assign CPU, memory, storage, supported GPU utilization or internal-battery charge to each ring.
• Show rings and numeric readings independently. Choose CPU, memory, disk read, disk write, upload and download numbers separately.
• Choose one direction for a clear single-row reading, or both for compact two-row readings with a shared MB/s unit.
• CPU and storage are green below 80%, yellow from 80% through 90%, and red above 90%. Memory colors follow macOS memory pressure.
• Click the menu bar to open the overview. Hover over or click hardware modules for details. Settings apply immediately and stay saved.

OPTIONAL COMPANION
App usage rankings and hardware temperatures require the separately downloaded PulseBar Helper. In PulseBar Settings, download the native macOS installer directly, open the downloaded PKG, and follow the system installation steps. Then choose Open Helper and Enable Helper. No GitHub page or dragging files is needed. Basic monitoring, charts, and performance events work without the helper. Sensor availability varies by Mac model and macOS version; temperatures are shown only for supported, valid readings.

LOCAL AND PRIVATE
No account, advertising, or monitoring-data collection. Readings and saved performance events stay on your Mac. Network monitoring reads system byte counters and does not inspect traffic content. The helper works only for your macOS user and does not require administrator privileges.

Requires macOS 13 or later. Supports Apple Silicon and Intel. The main app is updated through the App Store; the helper is distributed separately.
reviewNotes:
PulseBar is a menu bar system monitor. Click its menu bar readings to open the 2×2 equal-tile overview (CPU/GPU, memory, network, storage); hover over CPU or Memory for detail charts and top apps. The three rings and numeric directions are configurable in Settings. Clicking a detail no longer pins it. No login or in-app purchases are required.

The sandboxed app independently provides CPU, memory, disk/network rates, supported GPU/battery readings, history charts, and local performance events. App usage rankings and hardware temperatures use a separate, optional PulseBar Helper installed by the user outside the App Store. This is disclosed in the listing and app settings. The main app does not install the helper or change system services.

Helper installation: the Settings button opens the direct, version-pinned PKG URL in the default browser: https://github.com/monaco-io/PulseBar/releases/download/helper-v1.0.2/PulseBar-Helper.pkg . The main app does not download or execute code. The user opens the downloaded, signed and notarized PKG in macOS Installer, which places only the helper in the user’s Applications folder, without scripts or root privileges. The user returns to Settings, chooses Open Helper, and explicitly chooses Enable Helper. The installer does not launch or enable a service. If macOS requires background-item approval, the helper links to Login Items settings. Once enabled, the main app reconnects automatically. Choose Disable Helper in the helper app to unregister before removal. Closing its window alone leaves the registered service available.

The one temporary entitlement is com.apple.security.temporary-exception.mach-lookup.global-name, restricted to 45Y6A23PTN.io.github.monaco-io.PulseBar.HelperService. It is used only to request read-only app-usage and temperature samples from this developer's separately installed companion. Both ends enforce Apple signatures, team 45Y6A23PTN, exact bundle identifiers, and the same Unix user. The service accepts no commands, file paths, writes, or process-control operations. No root service or administrator access is used. Monitoring data stays on the Mac.

The App Store bundle excludes the process reader, SMC temperature reader, and Sparkle. The helper is not embedded in the store app. The store app is updated only by the App Store. If the helper is missing, rejected, disabled, or unresponsive, rankings/temperatures are unavailable and basic monitoring continues. Some sensors and GPU/battery readings depend on Mac hardware and macOS support.

Support and privacy: https://github.com/monaco-io/PulseBar/blob/main/docs/HELPER.md and https://github.com/monaco-io/PulseBar/blob/main/docs/PRIVACY.md
whatsNew: The overview now uses four equally sized tiles, with CPU and GPU readings together. Settings and More use matching native macOS controls. The optional PulseBar Helper now downloads directly as a standard macOS installer, with no GitHub page or manual dragging. The main app and future updates are distributed through the App Store.
